free_tier.stated: Lite plan, quoted from the FAQ: 'We also offer a Lite plan with 10 GB of storage and 10 hours of Pulse compute per month included. A credit card is not required to sign up for the free trial or use the Lite plan.' The plan card adds 'Up to 3 internal active users and 2 service accounts' and '10 hrs Pulse compute per month included'.

interface_detail: REST API, per the MotherDuck REST API page: "REST API reference for managing MotherDuck resources"
tooling: the provider documents its own "MotherDuck CLI", per the interfaces page
chaining: DuckDB over 10 GB of managed Parquet is the cheapest analytical layer found, and a local DuckDB client connects to it with the same SQL, so a query developed on the free tier runs unchanged anywhere.

limits.value: 10 Pulse compute-hours a month fails before the 10 GB of storage: Pulse is metered per query with a one-second minimum, so a dashboard refreshed every minute exhausts the hours while storage is still nearly empty.

identity_cost.detail: no card: the FAQ states 'A credit card is not required to sign up for the free trial or use the Lite plan', and the docs state 'Lite without a credit card includes 30 minutes per day at no charge'. No hold exists because no payment method is taken. The signup fields are not quoted, so the email requirement is inferred rather than read, and debit and prepaid acceptance are not stated.

evidence.quote: MotherDuck CLI: Drive MotherDuck from your terminal: run queries, build Dives and Flights, and script it all with JSON output.
REST API reference for managing MotherDuck resources including databases, users, and access tokens.

notes: The free tier is Pulse only: Standard, Jumbo and Mega instances require the Business plan. Without a card the plan is 'Lite (with limits)', capped at 30 minutes of Flight compute a day and no scheduling. Historical retention is 1 day on Lite, so time travel is not a backup.
